title: How many textbooks fit on the shelf?
description: Textbooks that are two point five centimetres thick are placed on a shelf one hundred and sixty centimetres long. The video divides the length of the shelf by the thickness of one book, using tenfold scaling to clear the decimal, and then asks whether any space is left.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number of equal pieces that fit in a length is the length divided by the size of one piece, and a decimal divisor is cleared by multiplying both numbers by ten. Ask the class how many books would fit if each were two centimetres thick before any work is shown. Watch for students who divide the thickness by the length.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q4
video_script.why: The child can divide one amount by another to get an amount for one, and now divides a length by a thickness with a decimal to count how many fit.
video_script.substitution: The length of the shelf is divided by the thickness of one book, after both are multiplied by ten so the divisor is a whole number.
video_script.anchor: A teacher, a bookshelf 160 cm long and textbooks 2.5 cm thick, with 80 textbooks wanted on the shelf
video_script.payoff_line: Sixty four textbooks fit and no space is left

final_answer.value: 64 textbooks; no space left (80 textbooks would need 200 cm)
final_answer.spoken: sixty four textbooks and no space left

maths_rules: 64 x 2.5 = 160, so 160 - 160 = 0 cm of space is left
80 x 2.5 = 200 cm, which is more than 160 cm, so 80 textbooks do not fit
video_script.design: One idea: length divided by thickness gives how many fit. The shelf and the book stay on the board all video; the working band builds in the idea part, from the division through the tenfold scaling to the check with eighty books.
open_questions: The book says textbooks; the worklist says books. The video says textbooks, as the book does.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='books'/>A teacher placed textbooks that are two point five centimetres thick on a bookshelf.
<bookmark mark='want'/>The teacher wanted to place eighty textbooks on the shelf.
<bookmark mark='shelf'/>The bookshelf is one hundred and sixty centimetres long.
How many textbooks could be placed? Was any space left, and if yes, how much?

beats.on_screen: Given: shelf 160 cm long; one book 2.5 cm thick; 80 textbooks wanted

marks.given: the three facts are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a shelf one hundred and sixty centimetres long. One book is two point five centimetres thick, and eighty are wanted.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many textbooks fit, and how much space is left

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many textbooks fit, and how much space is left.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, find how many textbooks fit.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide the shelf length by the thickness of one book. That is one hundred and sixty divided by two point five.

marks.times: times 10 is written on both numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step two, make the divisor a whole number. Multiply both numbers by ten.
<bookmark mark='new'/>One hundred and sixty becomes one thousand six hundred, and two point five becomes twenty five.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Step three, twenty five goes into one hundred four times.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>One thousand six hundred is sixteen hundreds.
<bookmark mark='prod'/>Each hundred holds four textbooks, and the division is sixteen times four.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the 80 textbooks: 80 × 2.5 = 200, and 200 > 160, so not all 80 fit

marks.cmp: 200 > 160 is written and the extra length hangs past the end of the shelf

narration: <bookmark mark='eighty'/>Step four, check the eighty textbooks the teacher wanted. They need eighty times two point five, which is two hundred centimetres.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>Two hundred is more than one hundred and sixty, so not all eighty fit.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 16 × 4 = 64 textbooks; 64 × 2.5 = 160 cm, so no space is left

marks.space: 64 × 2.5 = 160 is written and the shelf is shown full

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Sixty four textbooks fit and no space is left.
<bookmark mark='space'/>Sixty four times two point five is one hundred and sixty, which fills the shelf.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The space left is zero centimetres.
